# Semantic Reasoning and Deliberation\chaptersubtitle{Expiring Intent Leases, Kinematic Reachability, and Fallbacks}

![**Systems Organ Focus: Stage 4 (Semantic Deliberation & System 2 Expiring Intent Leases).** Stage 4 operates asynchronously on the Linux MPU at $0.5\text{--}2\text{ Hz}$, converting open-vocabulary natural language instructions into metric $SE(3)$ affordance targets wrapped in time-bounded validity leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) before handoff to System 1.5 motion planners.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch06 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an intelligent foundation model that correctly understands a human voice command command a robot arm to break its own joints against a wall?*

Large language and vision-language models possess extraordinary semantic competence: they can interpret complex natural language instructions, identify novel objects, and propose strategic task decompositions. In the physical world, however, pure semantic fluency is dangerously ungrounded. A foundation model has no intrinsic awareness of joint torque limits, Jacobian singularities, or physical reach boundaries. If raw model tokens are mapped directly to actuator setpoints, the result is mechanical destruction. In Physical AI, high-level models act exclusively as untrusted proposal engines—emitting time-bounded intent leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) that must be filtered through morphological reachability checks and dynamic scene freshness gates before physical execution is permitted.

By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Ground Open-Vocabulary Goals into Metric $SE(3)$ Affordance Frames:** Lift 2D vision-language patch tokens into calibrated 3D metric coordinate frames ($T_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$).
2. **Implement Morphological Reachability and Singularity Filters:** Screen untrusted foundation model proposals through geometric reachability envelopes ($\mathcal{W}_{\text{reach}}$), Jacobian condition numbers ($\kappa(J)$), and Yoshikawa manipulability indices.
3. **Deconstruct VLM Inference Dynamics:** Understand KV-cache dynamics, multimodal adapters, and tail latency spikes ($P_{99}$).
4. **Analyze Semantic Failures:** Break down the unbounded semantic reach autopsy where an ungrounded VLM shattered a harmonic drive.
5. **Enforce Expiring Intent Validity Leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$):** Structure time-bounded intent contracts that monitor dynamic scene drift and revoke physical authorization when timestamps expire.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Vision-language models provide broad open-world semantic competence, but have no intrinsic awareness of physical limits; they must act strictly as untrusted proposal engines emitting Time-Bounded Intent Leases filtered by kinematic reachability.

## Semantic Agency: Open-World Deliberation and Physical Grounding

In digital artificial intelligence, multimodal Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate astonishing capabilities. You can present a model with an image of a cluttered workbench, type the open-vocabulary prompt *"locate the rusted M8 bolt behind the heat sink,"* and watch the model generate accurate 2D bounding boxes, segmentation masks, and descriptive natural language responses.

In the digital world, software operates behind glass. If the model hallucinates an object that does not exist, misidentifies a reflection, or takes two seconds to generate its output, the error remains safely contained in memory: a bounding box is drawn in the wrong pixel location on a monitor, or an API returns an incorrect JSON string. You can adjust the prompt, lower the temperature, or re-run the query.

In Physical AI Systems, software moves physical mass and dissipates electrical energy. The moment you connect an autoregressive vision-language model to a physical robot arm, mobile rover, or automated assembly workcell, the model's outputs cease to be advisory text tokens. If a VLM hallucinates a 3D coordinate located ten centimeters beyond an arm's physical reach, the inverse kinematics solver will invert an ill-conditioned Jacobian matrix, joint velocities will spike toward infinity, and the arm will slam violently into its mechanical hardstops or a nearby glass fixture. If the model takes $800\text{ ms}$ to generate a grasp target while a human operator reaches into the workcell, the robot will execute an obsolete action based on a world state that no longer exists.

High-capacity multimodal models are indispensable for System 2 Semantic Deliberation—they provide the open-world semantic reasoning required to understand unstructured human instructions and complex visual scenes. However, they are untrusted proposal generators operating at human deliberation speeds ($0.5\text{--}2\text{ Hz}$). They possess zero intrinsic knowledge of motor dynamics, gear ratios, kinematic singularities, or physical momentum.

To harness the semantic power of foundation models without risking mechanical destruction, Physical AI architectures isolate the VLM behind a formal systems contract: the Expiring Intent Lease. Before any semantic proposal reaches downstream motion planners or actuator inverters, it must pass through rigorous geometric de-projection, morphological reachability filters, and real-time freshness validation.

## Affordance Grounding and Kinematic Reachability Corridors

When a reasoning engine identifies an interaction target, the semantic understanding must be grounded into a metric coordinate frame within the physical workspace.

### Lifting 2D Semantic Tokens into 3D Metric Affordance Frames
When a vision-language model predicts a spatial interaction point $(u, v)$ on an image plane, the reasoning engine lifts the 2D point into a metric 6-DoF target coordinate frame $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$:

$$\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} & \mathbf{p}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

The 3D position $\mathbf{p}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}}$ is computed by multiplying the inverse intrinsic camera matrix $\mathbf{K}^{-1}$ by depth $d(u, v)$ and transforming by the camera extrinsic pose $\mathbf{T}_{\text{camera}}^{\text{world}}$.

### 3D Bounding Hulls and Morphological Reachability

A proposed target $\mathbf{p}_{\text{target}}$ must reside strictly inside the robot's reachable workspace envelope $\mathcal{W}_{\text{reach}}$, effectively a 3D bounding hull representing the outer limits of kinematic feasibility:

$$\|\mathbf{p}_{\text{target}} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{base}}\| \le R_{\text{max}} - d_{\text{margin}}$$

Targets generated outside this 3D bounding hull are immediately rejected before passing to any downstream planner. 

### Jacobian Condition Number and Yoshikawa Manipulability Ellipses

Furthermore, approaching singular configurations near the workspace boundary causes joint velocities to explode, as the inverse kinematics solve involves inverting the Jacobian matrix ($\dot{\mathbf{q}} = \mathbf{J}^\dagger \dot{\mathbf{x}}$). The reasoning engine screens proposals using the **Yoshikawa Manipulability Index** ($w$) and the **Jacobian Condition Number** ($\kappa(\mathbf{J})$):

$$w(\mathbf{q}) = \sqrt{\det\left( \mathbf{J}(\mathbf{q}) \mathbf{J}^T(\mathbf{q}) \right)}, \qquad \kappa(\mathbf{J}) = \frac{\sigma_{\max}(\mathbf{J})}{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{J})}$$

The Yoshikawa manipulability index represents the volume of the manipulability ellipsoid; values approaching zero indicate the loss of a degree of freedom. The condition number $\kappa(\mathbf{J})$ indicates the error amplification when inverting the Jacobian. Proposals producing $w(\mathbf{q}) < w_{\text{min}}$ or $\kappa(\mathbf{J}) > \kappa_{\text{max}}$ (e.g., $\kappa > 50$) are rejected, restricting motion to safe kinematic reachability corridors.

## Vision-Language Models & Causal Intent Decoders

To understand why large models fail physically, we must examine their computational anatomy from first principles.

### Text Tokenization and Multimodal Projection

Modern VLMs process inputs not as physical dimensions, but as abstract discrete tokens. Text is processed using Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), mapping strings to integers. Visual information from camera sensors is divided into patches, processed by a vision encoder (like ViT), and projected into the same latent dimension as the text tokens via a multimodal projection adapter (typically a Multi-Layer Perceptron, or MLP). This aligns the visual embedding space with the linguistic embedding space, enabling joint reasoning.

### The Causal Transformer Decoder

At the core of the VLM lies the causal transformer decoder. In a causal (autoregressive) architecture, the model predicts the next token $x_{t+1}$ conditioned strictly on the preceding tokens $x_1, \dots, x_t$. The transformer uses scaled dot-product attention, allowing tokens to contextually integrate information from earlier in the sequence. However, this process is purely semantic—the model learns co-occurrence probabilities from internet-scale datasets, completely decoupled from the laws of physics. It does not integrate ordinary differential equations or understand mechanical impedance.

### KV-Cache Dynamics and Tail Latency Spikes ($P_{99}$)

Autoregressive token generation is memory-bandwidth bound. To avoid recomputing the attention matrix for the entire sequence at every step, inference engines maintain a Key-Value (KV) cache. As the generation sequence grows, the KV-cache expands linearly, leading to erratic memory access patterns. On edge silicon with constrained memory buses, this manifests as severe tail latency spikes ($P_{99}$ latency). A token generation that typically takes $100\text{ ms}$ might occasionally stall for $800\text{ ms}$ during memory paging or thermal throttling.

Because of this computational architecture—probabilistic autoregressive decoding subject to high $P_{99}$ latency—high-capacity VLMs must act strictly as untrusted proposal engines. They provide vital semantic direction but cannot guarantee temporal determinism or physical safety.

## Systems Failure Anatomy: The Unbounded Semantic Reach

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Unbounded Semantic Reach"}
**Platform:** 7-DoF Articulated Manipulator Workcell.
**Failure Mechanism:** Ingesting an open-vocabulary human voice command, the high-level VLM emitted a target coordinate $1.59\text{ m}$ away ($0.74\text{ m}$ beyond the robot's physical reach of $0.85\text{ m}$).
**Root Cause:** Inverting an ill-conditioned Jacobian ($\kappa(J) = 1{,}840$) near the workspace boundary without geometric reachability filtering caused joint velocities to explode ($\dot{q}_5 > 450^\circ/\text{s}$).
**Physical Consequence:** The wrist struck a polycarbonate safety barrier at $1.4\text{ m/s}$ ($2.1\text{ kN}$ shock load), cracking the partition and shearing the harmonic drive gear teeth ($5,400\text{ USD}$ damage).
:::

![The Precision Articulated Manipulator Workcell. Ingesting an open-vocabulary human voice command, the high-level foundation model emitted a goal coordinate $47\text{ cm}$ beyond the arm's physical reach envelope; attempting to invert the ill-conditioned Jacobian ($\kappa(J) = 1{,}840$) caused joint velocities to explode, ramming the wrist into a safety partition.](figures/fig06_manipulator_arm_cropped.jpg){#fig-intent-platform width=100%}

In the autopsy introduced in the prologue and detailed above, a 7-DoF manipulator received the voice command *"Retrieve the heated calibration bolt behind the fixture."* The VLM hallucinated a target coordinate at $\|\mathbf{p}_{\text{target}}\| = 1.59\text{ m}$, exceeding the arm's physical reach ($R_{\max} = 0.85\text{ m}$). 

Passing this un-screened target directly to the inverse kinematics solver caused the Jacobian condition number to explode to $\kappa(\mathbf{J}) = 1{,}840$. Joint 5 accelerated beyond rated limits ($\dot{q}_5 > 450^\circ/\text{s}$), swinging the wrist into a polycarbonate safety partition at $1.4\text{ m/s}$, inducing a $2.1\text{ kN}$ dynamic impact that sheared the harmonic drive flexspline.

| **$T + 0.000\text{ s}$** | Wrist / Polycarbonate Wall | Manipulator strikes safety partition at $1.4\text{ m/s}$ ($2.1\text{ kN}$ dynamic shock). | Harmonic drive teeth shear ($5,400\text{ USD}$ overhaul). |

## The Expiring Intent Lease Interface & Co-Design Checkpoint

To harness the VLM without granting it unvetted authority, the reasoning subsystem formalizes the **Time-Bounded Intent Lease** ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$). A high-level foundation model does not emit raw PWM voltages; it emits this structured contract:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \left\langle \text{TaskID}, \; \mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}}, \; \mathcal{W}_{\text{corridor}}, \; v_{\text{max}}, \; t_{\text{issued}}, \; t_{\text{expire}}, \; \gamma_{\text{confidence}} \right\rangle$$

* **Target Pose ($\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$):** The metric 3D goal coordinate.
* **Bounding Spatial Corridor ($\mathcal{W}_{\text{corridor}} \subset \mathbb{R}^3$):** A geometric volume (convex polyhedral prism) within which downstream trajectory planners are authorized to move.
* **Maximum Permissible Velocity ($v_{\text{max}}$):** A hard velocity ceiling derived from dynamic stopping limits.
* **Expiration Timestamp ($t_{\text{expire}} = t_{\text{issued}} + \tau_{\text{lease}}$):** A strict deadline (typically $200\text{--}500\text{ ms}$). If the downstream planner fails to complete the motion or renew the lease before $t_{\text{expire}}$, physical authority is revoked automatically.

### The 5-Column Matrix Checkpoint Audit

We conclude the Reasoning stage by auditing its resolution across all foundational physical constraints in a unified 5-column ledger (@tbl-intent-matrix-checkpoint):

| Physical Constraint | Systems Tension | Architectural Resolution | Parameter | Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Time & Freshness** | Slow VLM deliberation risks commanding obsolete actions against moving targets. | **Expiring Intent Leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$)** with hard Time-To-Live deadlines. | `lease.validity_duration_ms` | Timestamp expiry ($t > t_{\text{expire}}$) |
| **Inertia & Stopping** | High-level goals ignore moving mass and momentum requirements. | Bounded velocity corridors conditioned on dynamic stopping margins. | `trajectory.max_velocity` | Deceleration limit envelope |
| **Actuation & Jerk** | Singularity targets demand infinite joint acceleration from motors. | **Yoshikawa Manipulability** and Jacobian condition screening. | `singularity.max_condition` | $\kappa(\mathbf{J}) \le 50$, $w \ge 0.05$ |
| **Reach & Boundaries** | VLM hallucinates targets outside physical manipulator limits. | **Morphological reachability filters** via 3D bounding hulls. | `reachability.max_radius` | $R_{\text{max}} - d_{\text{margin}}$ |
| **Silicon Determinism** | KV-cache tail latency ($P_{99}$) stalls physical execution loops. | **Asynchronous Dual-Brain Decoupling:** Slow leases feed fast planners. | `confidence.min_threshold` | Fallback trigger on latency/ambiguity |

## Chapter Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter established how high-level semantic reasoning is grounded into metric physical action without risking mechanical destruction. High-capacity foundation models provide extraordinary open-world semantic comprehension, but their autoregressive architecture and variable latency mean they must act strictly as untrusted proposal generators.

By packaging high-level intent into Expiring Intent Leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) bounded by morphological 3D bounding hulls and restricted by Jacobian condition numbers ($\kappa(\mathbf{J}) \le 50$), we eliminate kinematic whiplash and ensure that semantic hallucinations never cause physical collisions.

In the following chapter, **Chapter 7 (Plan: Action Chunking, Diffusion Decoders, and Polynomial Splines)**, we explore how physical agents translate these time-bounded intent leases into smooth, dynamically feasible motor trajectories that bridge multi-millisecond computational delays and feed real-time torque controllers.
